heroHeadline: Project Freedom Launched and Paused; Rubio Declares Epic Fury Over; US-Iran One-Page Memo Within Reach — Day 68
heroSubtitle: Day 67 (May 5) brought the most consequential 24 hours of the conflict since the April 8 ceasefire: the US Navy launched 'Project Freedom,' escorting two commercial ships through the Strait of Hormuz under USS Truxtun and USS Mason — destroying seven IRGC fast boats in the process — while Secretary of State Rubio declared the 67-day Operation Epic Fury bombing campaign 'effectively over,' marking the formal end of large-scale US offensive strikes on Iranian territory. Iran fired IRGC warning shots at a US warship but stopped short of direct engagement with the escort convoy. Hours after the launch, Trump paused Project Freedom, citing 'great progress' toward a 'complete and final agreement,' while the naval blockade of Iranian ports remained fully in force. Iran struck a UAE oil facility, wounding three Indian nationals; the UAE engaged 15 missiles and 4 drones. The UK proscribed the IRGC as a terrorist organization. On Day 68 (May 6), Pakistan's mediators reported the US and Iran were 'closing in on a one-page memo' — a narrow framework focused on Hormuz and ceasefire terms, deferring the nuclear question entirely. Brent crude fell to ~$109.87/bbl on the deal signals, down from a $114.4 peak. Trump simultaneously threatened bombing 'at a much higher level and intensity than before the ceasefire' if no deal was reached, and again claimed hostilities 'terminated' to sidestep the War Powers Resolution. IAEA Director General Grossi confirmed no access to any of Iran's four enrichment facilities since February 28; Iran's enriched uranium stockpile (~200 kg at 60% purity) remains unaccounted at the Isfahan underground complex — a critical obstacle to any nuclear element in the one-page memo.
